results.title: LLM Agent Long-Term Memory Architectures - Medium
results.snippet: Core problem: LLMs lack persistent state. Memory architecture approaches: flat retrieval-based, explicitly structured, and policy-managed systems. Modern dual-store architectures combine vector database and knowledge graph.

results.title: Your Code Agent Can Grow Alongside You with Structured Memory - arXiv
results.snippet: Recent research on structured memory for code agents; demonstrates token efficiency improvements and retention mechanisms for multi-session continuity.

results.title: Best AI Agent Memory Systems in 2026: 8 Frameworks Compared - Vectorize
results.snippet: Comparative analysis of Mem0, Zep, Letta, Cognee, and others. Key metrics: extraction latency, semantic precision, decay/ranking algorithms, self-hosted options.

results.title: Always-On Agents: Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance - arXiv
results.snippet: Comprehensive survey on persistent memory architectures for long-running agents, governance patterns, and state consolidation techniques.

results.title: HyMem: Hybrid Memory Architecture with Dynamic Retrieval Scheduling - arXiv
results.snippet: Hybrid memory combining fast cache layer (core memory) with slow archival (long-term store). Relevance-based scheduling for what to promote/demote.

results.title: 7 MCP Server Best Practices for Scalable AI Integrations - MarkTechPost
results.snippet: MCP server design patterns: avoid 1:1 tool-to-endpoint mapping, grouping related operations, OAuth 2.0 for auth, read-only defaults, gateway pattern for multi-server orchestration.

results.title: Model Context Protocol - Best Practice Guide
results.snippet: Official MCP best practices: tool design principles, error handling, streaming, authentication patterns, deployment scaling patterns.

results.title: Cross-Encoder Reranking for Semantic Search - Medium
results.snippet: Cross-encoders process query+document jointly for semantic reranking. Outperforms bi-encoders on relevance; adds 50-100ms latency. LLM-based rerankers (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet) now stronger than traditional cross-encoders.

results.title: Advanced RAG Retrieval: Cross-Encoders & Reranking - Towards Data Science
results.snippet: Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense + cross-encoder) architecture. RRF fusion strategy. Current production best practice: semantic search + LLM reranking, effective at scale.

results.title: Mem0 vs Zep vs Letta vs Cognee - Practical Comparison - DEV Community
results.snippet: Detailed 2026 comparison: Mem0 (fast setup, auto-extraction cost), Zep (temporal KG, summarization, production-grade), Letta (agent-managed memory, long-horizon), Cognee (knowledge graph reasoning). Decision matrix by use case.

results.title: Ebbinghaus Forgetting Curve for AI Agent Memory - DEV Community
results.snippet: Implementation of Ebbinghaus forgetting curve decay in agent memory. FadeMem biologically-inspired architecture with differential decay rates by semantic relevance and access frequency.

results.title: MemGuard: Preventing Memory Contamination in LLM-Augmented Agents - arXiv
results.snippet: Safety: preventing stale/contradictory memories from harming agent outputs. Memory versioning and conflict resolution strategies.

results.title: Hybrid RAG: Graphs, BM25, and End of Black-Box Retrieval - NetApp
results.snippet: Production hybrid RAG combining BM25 (lexical), dense vectors, and knowledge graphs. GraphRAG paradigm emerging as standard for complex retrieval.

tangential_findings.title: AutoMem (open-source alternative)
tangential_findings.note: MIT licensed, FalkorDB + Qdrant backend. 70.69% on LoCoMo benchmark (beats Mem0 base 66.9%). < 100ms lookups. Mentioned in Mem0 article comments as overlooked alternative.

tangential_findings.title: Memory governance gap across all systems
tangential_findings.note: Mem0/Zep/Letta/Cognee handle user interaction memory well but none manage upstream knowledge base freshness. Stale/conflicting documents cause bad outputs despite perfect episodic memory. PromptOwl governance layer addressing this (97% vs 90-93% quality under stale-doc conditions).

tangential_findings.title: Memory decay via value retirement (Enki)
tangential_findings.note: Alternative to Ebbinghaus: retire old values at write-time (current value only comes back). Reduces storage footprint ~50%. Complementary to rank-based decay; addresses storage/latency axis rather than recall accuracy.

tangential_findings.title: BECOMER framework (LLM-agnostic memory)
tangential_findings.note: 94.4% LongMemEval score with zero tokens (vs Mem0's 6,787). Suggests structural memory (not vector-based) can match dense retrieval. Potential architecture lesson for Nexus on reducing embedding/retrieval overhead.
